claims.text: No unicode box-drawing, no fancy glyphs: only ``+ - |`` so it prints on a raw Windows console.
claims.why: The helper functions _rule and _row use only '+', '-', '|', and spaces.

claims.text: "hand_reachable" recall is partly self-graded and MUST NOT be blended with independently-derived recall into one headline number.
claims.why: The code defines _PROVENANCE_NOTE with a disclaimer for 'hand_reachable' but does not contain logic that prevents blending; blending prevention is outside this chunk.

claims.text: PARTIALLY SELF-GRADED: a human picked these labels AND verified them reachable by running the same slicer being graded. Treat this recall as an upper bound / sanity check, NOT independent proof the slicer works.
claims.why: This is a claim about the provenance of labels; the code only defines the string, does not enforce or verify the behaviour.

claims.text: INDEPENDENT: labels derived from what an on-disk diff literally changed -- no graph walk involved. This recall is not self-graded.
claims.why: Same as above; claim about label derivation, not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: INDEPENDENT: labels derived from git co-change (files that change together) -- no graph walk involved. This recall is not self-graded.
claims.why: Same as above; claim about label derivation.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD (lane A1) -- honest, ASCII-only accounting for tasks where the unconditional secret floor fail-closed on the task's OWN focus file (see harness._is_focus_withheld / slice.py's FOCUS GATE). Neither a pass (no slice text was ever compared to must_include) nor a recall miss (the label was never even attempted) -- its own bucket, excluded from every mean/count above. Absent (result.get) for any hand-built result dict that predates this field, and adds no lines when there are none.
claims.why: The function uses result.get('focus_withheld_ids') and returns empty list if absent or empty; it returns lines with header and IDs; it does not add lines if none.

claims.text: Shared renderer for the "PROVENANCE BREAKDOWN" block used by both Tier 1 and the arms report. Always shows both tiers (even when empty) and always prints the honesty note -- this block is the deliverable of this sprint.
claims.why: The function always prints the 'PROVENANCE BREAKDOWN' header, the honesty note for each provenance, and includes both 'primary' and 'quarantine' tiers in the loop. It is called from both render_tier1 and render_arms.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall/compression/slice_tokens/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they get their own ERRORED section below, not a row in this recall/compression table. FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (see harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section below.
claims.why: The function skips tasks with 'error' in t or t.get('focus_withheld') when building rows; errored tasks are later added in a separate section via result.get('errored').

claims.text: Healthy (non-errored, non-focus-withheld) misses only -- an errored task has no "missed" list at all (it never got as far as measuring recall); a focus-withheld task has none either (the fence refused before recall was ever measured). Both are reported in their own unmissable sections, not folded in here as a miss.
claims.why: The misses list filters tasks with 'error' not in t and not t.get('focus_withheld') and t['missed'] non-empty; errored and focus-withheld are excluded.

claims.text: ERRORED section -- a per-task resolution failure (bad repo label, or a target no longer in the index -- e.g. a quarantined mint task whose file moved) is EXCLUDED from every mean above but must never go unreported: "a degraded measurement is reported, never silent." Absent entirely (result.get, not result[...]) for any pre-existing caller that hand-built a Tier-1 result dict without this key -- and always absent when there are zero errored tasks, so this block adds NO lines to that report.
claims.why: The code uses result.get('errored') or [] and only adds lines if non-empty; it adds a header and lists tasks.

claims.text: A/B/C: distilled slice vs whole-repo concat vs BM25 retrieval. Model-free (recall via substring match, no LLM), so this runs offline every time.
claims.why: The docstring claims model-free recall via substring match; the function does not contain that logic, it only formats results. Verification requires the harness code.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall_A/tokens_A/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they are reported in their own section below, not in this table. FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section.
claims.why: The function filters healthy tasks excluding those with 'error' or 'focus_withheld'; errored tasks are later processed via result.get('errored').

claims.text: c_beats_a is tie-inclusive (recall_C >= recall_A, see harness.eval_task_arms) so this block -- not the "no" cells under the C>=A column -- is where a tie surfaces. A tie ("BM25 matches the product's recall at equal cost") is the commercially damning case, not merely a strict loss for A.
claims.why: The claim about tie-inclusive definition is in a comment; the code uses t['c_beats_a'] which is set elsewhere; the function only formats the output.

claims.text: ERRORED section -- same rationale as render_tier1's: excluded from every arm/aggregate above, never silently dropped. Absent when there are none.
claims.why: The code uses result.get('errored') or [] and adds lines only if non-empty.
